## Methods

### Study design

A phase I, single‐center, first‐in‐human, randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled study of garadacimab in healthy male adult volunteers was carried out between October 28, 2016, and September 22, 2017, in Adelaide, Australia (ACTRN 12616001438448). The study design is outlined in Figure [ref-type: supplementary-material] S1. Planned enrollment was six healthy male volunteers per each of the eight cohorts, with a total study population of 48 volunteers.

Garadacimab i.v. doses were 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, and 10 mg/kg administered via infusion over 60 minutes. Garadacimab s.c. doses were 1, 3, and 10 mg/kg administered via s.c. injection into the abdomen. The doses in this study were selected based on data obtained from in vitro nonclinical pharmacologic and toxicology studies.

A total of six volunteers received garadacimab or placebo in a ratio of 2:1 in each cohort. Sentinel dosing was implemented for each i.v. cohort and the first (1 mg/kg) s.c. cohort, and enrollment was staggered between cohorts (Figure [ref-type: supplementary-material] S1). --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Abstract

BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Iptacopan is an orally administered proximal complement inhibitor targeting factor B to selectively inhibit the alternative pathway of the complement system, while sparing activity of the classical pathway. Previous studies have shown that iptacopan is rapidly absorbed, reaching maximum concentration in approximately 1-2 h, and that dose-exposure proportionality is achieved after multiple doses of 100 mg and 200 mg twice daily (BID). The approved clinical dose is 200 mg BID. This study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of multiple supratherapeutic doses of iptacopan (400 and 800 mg BID) in healthy adult participants.

METHODS: The trial was a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blinded phase 1 multiple-ascending-dose study conducted in two sequential cohorts.

RESULTS: A total of 26 participants were randomized 2:1 to BID iptacopan 400 mg or 800 mg for 14 days or matching placebo; 24 participants completed the study. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were mild to moderate, and there were no serious AEs, deaths, or discontinuations due to AEs. The most frequent TEAE was headache, occurring in five (20.8%) participants. Plasma measures of iptacopan exposure appeared to increase in a dose-proportional manner, and biomarker analyses showed that there was rapid, near-complete, and persistent inhibition of alternative pathway activity for both doses, measured by the Wieslab assay.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings show that iptacopan supratherapeutic doses of 400 mg and 800 mg BID are well tolerated in healthy participants and describe the PK and PD properties of iptacopan and inhibition of the alternative complement pathway.

# METHODS

## Study design

- A first-in-human, Phase 1 study to assess the safety, tolerability, PK, and PD of iptacopan in healthy participants, 18–55 years of age.
- The study consisted of three parts: a single-ascending dose (SAD) study, a multiple-ascending dose (MAD) study, and a food-effect evaluation study.
- In the SAD phase (Figure 2A), eligible participants were randomized in a 3:1 ratio to receive a single dose of iptacopan (5 mg, 10 mg, 25 mg, 50 mg, 100 mg, 200 mg, or 400 mg) or placebo.
- In the MAD phase (Figure 2B), eligible participants were randomized in a 3:1 ratio to receive iptacopan (25 mg, 50 mg, 100 mg, or 200 mg) or matched placebo over a 14-day administration period.
  - On Days 1–13, participants received BID dosing; on Day 14, participants received only one dose.
  - A 5-day follow-up period included three follow-up evaluations and an EoS visit.

## Plasma Bb and safety assessments

- Circulating plasma Bb concentrations were measured using a validated immunoassay.
  - In the SAD phase, plasma Bb was measured at 10 timepoints (up to 48 hours after iptacopan administration).
